text:
Aisha: Quick Q — we need a short, compatible behaviour spec for 429 responses across hosted/dedicated/private. Two parts: (1) which headers to include so older clients keep working, and (2) what to do for overlapping per-route vs global quotas and burst smoothing.

Aisha: Example we currently emit sometimes:
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1767501200
```
Is that good enough or do we need an extra Redwood-specific header to indicate scope?

Ben: Short answer: keep Retry-After for backward compat (seconds or HTTP-date). Also always include X-RateLimit-* (limit, remaining, reset) for clients that parse those. For scope, add X-Redwood-Quota-Scope: route|global to avoid guesswork.

Caroline: Agreed. Two gotchas: (a) clients that only look for Retry-After will treat any 429 as fully blocked — so make Retry-After the min wait the client should use (i.e., the longest of route/global reset). (b) Reset should be epoch seconds (UTC) to avoid parsing differences.

Dana: For burst smoothing (we buffer/queue small bursts instead of immediate 429), how do we signal that? Should we still return 429 or 202 + header?

Ben: We should stick to 429 for rejected requests. For requests we accept but delay, we already stream progress; for queued we return 202 Accepted + X-Redwood-Queue-Delay: <seconds>. But keep it separate from quota 429 semantics.

Aisha: So the recommended surface: always include Retry-After (seconds), X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch secs), and X-Redwood-Quota-Scope. For queued-but-accepted responses include 202 + X-Redwood-Queue-Delay. Sounds good?

Caroline: SGTM. One more: when both per-route and global are exceeded, send Retry-After equal to max(route_retry, global_retry) and set X-Redwood-Quota-Scope: global,route (order by severity). Also set X-RateLimit-Limit to the limiting bucket, and Remaining=0.

Ben: +1. Also: document backoff guidance in the client docs — exponential backoff jitter starting at Retry-After, but fallback to 1s if header missing. Link to RFC: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-7.1.3

rate-limit-bot: integ/rate-limit-headers tests failed on main: parser expects Retry-After present for 429 in hosted mode. See CI log: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234

Ben: I'll send a test-fix PR to make tests accept X-RateLimit-Reset epoch secs and require Retry-After.

Dana: Will any of this break older mobile clients that only check X-RateLimit-Remaining? They sometimes ignore Retry-After.

Caroline: If clients ignore Retry-After, Remaining=0 + Reset epoch will be the fallback. Mobile clients that poll should look at Reset. We should add a short compatibility note in the /docs/rate-limits page.

Aisha: I'll draft the docs and the compatibility matrix (mobile web SDK, server SDKs, curl). I'll also add the header names and examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1287 (WIP)

Ben: Ping me once PR is ready, I'll update integration tests.

Aisha: Thanks — will follow up with the doc + spec. :pray:
